A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CONGO research project. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables, and figures, support comparison despite substantial revisions.

before.justification: v1 reports original quadratic-optimization experiments, Jackson-network simulations, and SocialNetwork microservice deployment results in Sections 6–7.

after.justification: v2 reports original experiments across the same task families, plus empirical convexity/sparsity characterization and recovery-runtime, sensitivity, and gradient-limit analyses.

M1.justification: v1 proposes one algorithm using combined Gaussian-row perturbations, averaging, and constrained basis pursuit. v2 develops B/Z/E variants: Z and E use individual-row perturbations and CoSaMP recovery, with Bernoulli and Gaussian matrices respectively. The B variant also revises perturbation and measurement normalization; this is more than renaming the original algorithm.

E1.justification: The quadratic-optimization, 15/50-queue Jackson-network, and SocialNetwork task families remain. v2 adds explicitly noise-corrupted quadratic function evaluations alongside noiseless evaluations in Figure 2, extending observation conditions within an existing task.

E2.justification: Comparisons across all three task families now distinguish CONGO-B, CONGO-Z, and CONGO-E, including the newly evaluated ZORO-derived variant. SGDBO is removed from both Jackson-network and real-system comparisons. GD/GDSP, NSGD/SGDSP, and PPO remain in their corresponding experiments.

E3.justification: Quadratic experiments change coefficient distributions, the constraint radius from 1000 to 100, the higher-dimensional configuration from 200 to 100, and sampling/smoothing settings. Jackson experiments revise sampling budgets, learning-rate schedules, workload parameters, and perturbation size from 0.02 to 0.5. Real-system results are evaluated against wall-clock time instead of rounds. These changes prevent treating replacement curves as matched-setting performance gains.

E4.justification: v2 adds empirical convexity/sparsity checks, noisy-oracle tests, basis-pursuit versus CoSaMP runtime analysis, a measurement-count sensitivity sweep, and an ablation of the gradient-magnitude limit. Appendices E–F investigate recovery failures, including unexplained error spikes. v1's separate comparison using five CONGO samples versus twenty GDSP samples is not retained.

E5.justification: v1 reports 50 seeds for 50-dimensional quadratic experiments and 10 for the 200-dimensional experiment; v2 reports 50 seeds throughout its revised quadratic study. This does not establish increased replication of an identical experiment. Mean/standard-deviation reporting, five Jackson-network seeds, and four real-system runs remain. v2 additionally reports an execution-time CDF over 1000 executions.

E6.justification: The principal experimental curves are replaced and expanded with B/Z/E results. In v2's revised quadratic experiments, Z and E closely track full-gradient descent while B performs worse; system results emphasize E's faster cost reduction. New findings include recovery-runtime differences, error spikes at m = 13–15, and reduced accumulated cost from enforcing the gradient limit. Changed methods and settings preclude direct numerical improvement claims over v1.

T1.justification: v1's O(s sqrt(log(d/s)) sqrt(T log(T+1))) regret result is replaced by a general expected-regret theorem and variant-specific O(sqrt(T)) guarantees. v2 adds measurement-error and restricted-isometry recovery derivations, claiming O(s log(d/s) + log(T)) evaluations per round for Z/E. Appendix C substantially replaces the earlier proofs; v1's sampling-budget corollary and perturbation-magnitude theorem are not retained.

C1.justification: The central contribution changes from one sparsity-exploiting algorithm with near-optimal regret to a framework supporting three algorithms, optimal time-horizon scaling, and dimension-independent regret. Sample-efficient Z/E variants become central contributions, and the principal practical superiority claim shifts to CONGO-E.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations linking B's performance to measurement interference, Z/E differences to measurement-matrix distributions, and recovery choice to runtime. It discusses unexplained undersampling failures and the requirement for known gradient/smoothness bounds. Exact-sparsity and queue-stability caveats remain; v1's basis-pursuit overhead concern is developed into the CoSaMP justification in Appendix E.

D1.justification: v2 supplies recovery tolerances and iteration limits, bound-estimation formulas, variant-specific implementation information and hyperparameter tables, and source-file/dependency details for the ZORO-derived implementation. It adds a repository access pointer for CONGO-Z/CoSaMP and removes SGDBO's implementation and pseudocode. Much existing hardware and deployment documentation is retained in Appendix G.

R1.justification: v2 substantially reframes the contribution around adapting Borkar's method and Cai et al.'s ZORO from fixed-objective optimization to OCO. It adds substantive discussion and citations for CoSaMP, basis pursuit, and multipoint-feedback guarantees. The SGDBO-related Tamiya and Yamasaki citation is removed. This changes research positioning beyond bibliographic restyling.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, motivating example, method exposition, and conclusion are extensively rewritten around the framework narrative. Section 4 gains a four-step organization and variant construction; appendices are reorganized from A–C into A–G, with existing experimental details moved to G. The title is shortened and citation style changes to author–date.

P2.justification: The timeline figure is removed, new convexity/sparsity panels are introduced, and the main experimental plots are redrawn with revised panels and legends. Real-system plots switch from rounds to seconds. New runtime, sensitivity, and ablation displays appear in Figures 5–7, and hyperparameter tables are restructured. The network and deployment diagrams are retained and relocated.

improvement.justification: v2 adds useful recovery-choice evidence and failure diagnostics absent from v1. However, its revised CONGO-B theory contains consequential inconsistencies: Equation 13 with delta = 1/(3LT) implies a T-squared sampling factor, while Theorem 2 reports T; Algorithm 2's perturbation normalization also differs from Appendix B and Lemma 1. These conflicts affect theoretical support and reproducibility, preventing a reliable overall quality judgment despite the empirical and explanatory gains.
